md_description: This workflow captures soil-derived bacterial strains, their genome sequencing and computational biosynthetic gene cluster analysis, and the chemical characterization of antibiotics produced by those clusters. It combines genomic localization and gene-level annotation with metabolite measurement to support discovery of novel antibiotic compounds and interpretation of their biosynthetic genetics.

soil_sample.reasoning: The soil_sample node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic provenance and environmental source fields that describe the sample itself, not collection procedures, downstream isolation, sequencing, or chemistry. Because no already_generated fields were provided, there was no need to exclude overlaps for this node. I focused on minimal identifiers and origin descriptors needed to interpret the source material for later bacterial isolation and genomic/metabolomic work.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the soil sample used as the source material for bacterial isolation; string format example: SOIL-001. Assigned at sample intake and used to link all downstream isolates and omics data back to the same environmental specimen.

Human-readable name of the collection site for the soil specimen, recorded at sampling time; example: forest edge plot A or agricultural field margin. Use to distinguish multiple soil sources within the study.
Date the soil sample was collected from the environment, recorded at the time of field sampling; format YYYY-MM-DD. Needed to interpret temporal context and storage age.

Free-text or coded location description for the soil collection site, recorded at sampling time; example: latitude/longitude pair, GPS coordinate string, or site label. Use to document the environmental origin of the sample.
Depth below the soil surface from which the sample was taken, measured during collection; typical range 0-100 cm. Record as a numeric depth in centimeters to capture the sampled soil horizon.

General soil classification or field-described soil type for the collected sample, recorded at collection; examples: loam, clay, sandy loam, silt. Use to describe the physical source environment of the isolates.

Brief description of the environmental habitat where the soil was collected, recorded at sampling; examples: forest soil, grassland soil, agricultural soil, rhizosphere-adjacent soil, wetland margin. Use to capture ecological context relevant to microbial origin.

isolated_bacterial_strains.reasoning: The isolated_bacterial_strains node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the cultured isolates: identity, taxonomic/phenotypic description, and origin from the upstream soil sample. I excluded strain isolation protocol details because those belong on the strain_isolation Process node, and I did not include sequencing, DNA, metabolite, or analysis outputs because those belong downstream. No already_generated fields were provided here, so no exclusions were needed on that basis.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier assigned to each cultured bacterial isolate; string format example: STR-001. Assigned after isolation and used to link genome and metabolite data back to the same strain.

Identifier of the upstream soil sample from which the isolate was obtained; string format example: SOIL-001. Record at strain curation to preserve provenance from environmental source to cultured isolate.
Laboratory label or accession used for the cultured strain, as maintained in the collection; example: isolate A12 or strain B-7. Useful when multiple aliases exist for the same isolate.

Best available taxonomic identification for the cultured isolate at the time of dataset creation, based on preliminary or final classification; examples: genus or species name. Record as currently accepted name if available, otherwise higher-level assignment.
Assessment of whether the cultured isolate is pure or mixed at the time it enters downstream analysis, recorded after colony purification and quality check; allowed values indicate the culture state.

Observable colony or culture morphology of the isolate, recorded during curation; examples: colony color, texture, shape, or filamentous appearance. Use to describe the living isolate itself rather than the isolation method.
Biosafety handling classification associated with the cultured isolate, recorded at laboratory registration; examples: BSL-1 or BSL-2. Useful for safe reuse and handling of the strain.

strain_isolation.reasoning: The strain_isolation node is a Process, so I included only how the microbiological isolation was performed and key outcome-quality indicators for that operation. I excluded intrinsic properties of the soil sample and cultured strains because those belong to Entity nodes, and I excluded downstream isolate identifiers and omics outputs because those are not produced by the process itself. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no duplicates to avoid for this node.

md_schema.descr: Microbiological strategy used to separate bacterial strains from the soil sample, recorded for the isolation step; examples: serial dilution plating, spread plating, enrichment culture, selective medium isolation, or heat shock enrichment. Use to describe the operational approach applied to the environmental material.

Primary growth medium or selective medium used during strain isolation, recorded at the time of processing; example: nutrient agar, R2A, ISP2, or custom selective medium. Use to document the culture conditions that enabled recovery of isolates.

Incubation temperature used during the isolation step, measured in degrees Celsius and recorded as the process was run; typical range 4-45. Include the temperature used to recover colonies or enrichment cultures from soil-derived material.

Duration of the isolation incubation period, measured in days from plating or enrichment setup to colony recovery or enrichment observation; typical range 1-30. Record the value used for this isolation workflow.
Oxygen availability used during strain isolation, recorded during culture setup; allowed values indicate whether the isolation was performed under aerobic, anaerobic, or microaerophilic conditions.

Outcome quality indicator for the isolation process, assessed after colony purification or enrichment; allowed values summarize whether the step yielded clean single colonies, mixed enrichments, or uncertain recovery.

genomic_dna_prep.reasoning: The genomic_dna_prep node is a Process, so I included only extraction/preparation parameters and a process-level quality indicator. I excluded isolate identity and strain provenance because those belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings and raw-read properties because they belong downstream to Capture and Signal nodes. No already_generated fields were provided, so there were no duplicate-name constraints to apply here.

md_schema.descr: Method used to extract genomic DNA from isolated bacterial strains, recorded for the preparation step; examples: phenol_chloroform, silica_column_kit, magnetic_bead_kit, or cetyltrimethylammonium_bromide (CTAB) extraction. Use to describe how DNA was obtained before sequencing.
Final DNA elution volume after purification, measured at the end of genomic DNA preparation in microliters; typical range 10-200. Record the volume of prepared DNA available for sequencing input.

Concentration of the prepared genomic DNA measured after extraction and cleanup, just before sequencing library input; typical range 0-1000 ng/ul. Use the concentration assay result for sequencing-ready DNA.

Spectrophotometric purity ratio of the prepared DNA measured after extraction and cleanup, typically near 1.8 for relatively pure DNA. Record the A260/A280 value used to assess suitability for sequencing.

Assessment of DNA fragment integrity or size distribution after preparation, recorded before sequencing library construction; examples: high_molecular_weight, partially_sheared, degraded. Use to capture suitability of DNA for genome sequencing.

Overall quality indicator for the genomic DNA preparation process, assessed after extraction and cleanup and before sequencing; allowed values summarize whether the preparation met sequencing input requirements.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the sequencing-ready genomic DNA aliquot; string format example: DNA-001. Assigned after preparation and used to connect the DNA material to subsequent sequencing.
Identifier of the bacterial strain from which this genomic DNA was prepared; string format example: STR-001. Record at DNA curation to preserve provenance from isolate to sequencing input.
Integrity status of the prepared DNA material at storage or handoff to sequencing; allowed values describe whether the DNA is intact enough for read generation.

Storage condition of the prepared genomic DNA before sequencing, recorded at the time of handoff or storage; examples: 4_celsius_short_term, minus_20_celsius, minus_80_celsius, or lyophilized. Use to capture how the DNA was preserved.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for the capture session; example: Illumina. Record the hardware vendor for the actively configured acquisition system.
Model of the sequencing instrument used for genomic read capture; example: NovaSeq 6000 or NextSeq 2000. Record the specific platform used for raw read acquisition.
Serial number or asset tag of the sequencing instrument used in the capture session; string format example: SN123456 or facility asset ID. Record to uniquely identify the hardware instance.
Unique identifier for the sequencing run or capture session; string format example: RUN-2026-001. Assigned at instrument operation time to link the capture settings to the generated raw reads.

Sequencing flow cell type used during the capture session, recorded as the actively selected hardware consumable; examples: S4, SP, or PE flow cell variants depending on the instrument. Use to document acquisition configuration.

Configured read length in base pairs for each sequencing read, set on the instrument before acquisition; typical values include 75, 100, 150, or 250 bp. Record the intended read length for the capture session.
Sequencing mode used for the capture session, recorded as an instrument setting; examples: single-end or paired-end. Use to document how reads were acquired from the prepared DNA.
Overall quality indicator for the sequencing capture session, assessed at the end of the run; allowed values summarize whether the instrument operation produced usable raw readout.

I excluded capture settings and upstream DNA properties because they belong elsewhere, and I removed read_length_bp because you flagged it as already generated in a previous DAG step. md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw sequencing read file or file set; string format example: FASTQ-001. Assigned when the FASTQ-like output is written and used to track the artifact.
Technical file format of the raw read artifact, recorded at storage time; examples: FASTQ, gzipped FASTQ, or interleaved FASTQ. Use to describe the on-disk representation of the sequencing data.
Total size of the raw read file or file set in bytes, measured when the artifact is deposited or transferred. Typical range depends on run scale and can span 10^6 to 10^11 bytes.
Number of individual reads contained in the raw sequencing artifact, counted from the FASTQ-like output after capture. Use this as a technical dimension of the raw data file.

File path, URI, or object-storage location where the raw read artifact is stored; example: s3://bucket/run1/FASTQ-001.gz or /data/raw_reads/sample1.fastq.gz. Record the retrieval location for the raw data file.

Technical quality summary of the raw reads computed from the file itself, such as mean Phred score or percent bases above Q30, recorded after file generation. Use to capture the raw data quality without interpretation of biology.

read_processing.reasoning: The read_processing node is a Process node, so I included only computational trimming/filtering parameters, software identity, and a process-level output quality indicator. I excluded raw-read file properties and instrument settings because those belong to the Signal and Capture nodes, and I excluded assembled-genome or downstream analysis outputs because those belong to later Derivative nodes. I also avoided the previously generated read_length_bp field due to the reported DAG-wide collision constraint.

md_schema.descr: Name of the read-processing software used for trimming and filtering raw sequencing reads; example: fastp. Record the computational tool that performed the transformation.
Version of the read-processing software used during this step; example: 0.23.2. Record the exact version to support reproducibility of the trimming and filtering operation.

Repository or distribution source for the read-processing software, recorded for reproducibility; examples: GitHub URL, Bioconda package name, or container registry reference. Use to identify the implementation used in processing.
Whether adapter trimming was enabled during read processing, recorded at process execution time; true if adapter sequences were removed before downstream analysis, false otherwise.
Minimum per-base quality threshold used to trim or filter reads, expressed as a Phred score integer; typical values 15-30. Record the setting applied during processing.
Minimum retained read length after trimming, expressed in base pairs and configured during read processing; typical values 30-100 bp. Use to document the cutoff below which reads were discarded.

Fraction of raw reads retained after processing, computed at the end of the trimming/filtering step; typical range 0.0-1.0. Use as a process-level output quality indicator for how much usable data remained.

processed_reads.reasoning: The processed_reads node is a Signal node, so I kept only artifact-specific fields that were not already generated elsewhere in the DAG. I excluded file_format, file_size_bytes, read_count, storage_uri, and quality_score_summary because you reported those IDs already exist in prior steps. I also excluded processing parameters, software, and assembly outputs because they belong to upstream Process nodes or downstream Derivative nodes, not this raw/processed data artifact layer.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the processed sequencing read file or file set; string format example: PROCFASTQ-001. Assigned when the trimmed and filtered read artifact is written and used to track the data product.

Mean read length in base pairs across the processed reads, computed from the trimmed read file after filtering; typical range 30-300 bp. Record the average length of the retained reads as a data-property summary.

Fraction of processed reads or bases still containing adapter signal after trimming, estimated from the processed file as a technical residual-quality metric; typical range 0.0-1.0. Use to assess the effectiveness of read cleanup.

Fraction of bases in the processed reads that are G or C, computed from the read file after trimming and filtering; typical range 0.0-1.0. Record as a technical composition summary of the processed sequence data.

Fraction of reads in the processed file that are exact or near-exact duplicates, estimated from the processed artifact after read cleanup; typical range 0.0-1.0. Use as a technical measure of redundancy in the retained reads.

Assessment of whether paired-end reads remain synchronized after processing, evaluated on the processed read artifact; allowed values indicate whether pairs are fully retained, partially broken, or unknown.

genome_assembly.reasoning: The genome_assembly node is a Process node, so I included only computational assembly parameters, software identity, and assembly-quality indicators. I excluded upstream processed-read artifact properties because those belong to the Signal node, and I excluded downstream draft-genome properties such as contig statistics or annotation outputs because those belong to the Derivative node. md_schema.descr: Name of the genome assembler used to reconstruct the draft bacterial genome from processed reads; example: SPAdes. Record the computational tool that performed the assembly.
Version of the genome assembly software used during this step; example: 3.15.5. Record the exact version to support reproducibility of the assembly process.

Repository or distribution source for the genome assembly software, recorded for reproducibility; examples: GitHub URL, Bioconda package name, or container registry reference. Use to identify the implementation used in assembly.

K-mer sizes used by the assembler during genome reconstruction, specified as a comma-separated list or array-like string; typical values depend on read length and can include multiple integers such as 21,33,55,77. Record the parameterization applied during assembly.
Minimum contig length retained by the assembly pipeline, measured in base pairs and configured during assembly output filtering; typical values 500-1000 bp. Use to document contig filtering criteria.

Assembly strategy or mode used by the assembler, recorded as a pipeline setting; examples: isolate, metagenome, or careful mode depending on software support. Use to describe how the reconstruction was performed.

Overall quality indicator for the assembly process, assessed after reconstruction and filtering; allowed values summarize whether the draft genome met expected continuity and completeness thresholds for downstream analysis.

draft_genome.reasoning: The draft_genome node is a Derivative node, so I included only computed genome-product properties: assembly identity, contig structure, continuity/completeness summaries, and storage/access details. I excluded assembly software and parameters because those belong to the upstream genome_assembly Process node, and I excluded BGC prediction or annotation outputs because those belong to later Derivative nodes. I also avoided previously generated file-level fields such as file_format, file_size_bytes, read_count, storage_uri, and quality_score_summary because those collide across the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the assembled draft genome product; string format example: GNM-001. Assigned after assembly and used to track the genome object into BGC prediction and annotation.

Public or internal accession for the draft genome assembly, if assigned; string format example: GCA_123456789.1 or facility-local assembly ID. Record the assembly reference used to share or retrieve the genome.
Number of contigs in the draft genome assembly, counted after reconstruction and filtering. Use as a structural summary of genome fragmentation.

Total length of the draft genome assembly in base pairs, computed from the assembled contigs after filtering; typical values for bacterial genomes are roughly 1e6-1e7 bp. Record the assembled genome span.

N50 contig length in base pairs for the draft genome assembly, calculated from the assembled contigs; typical bacterial draft genomes may range from 1e4 to 1e6 bp. Use this as a continuity metric of the derivative genome product.
Estimated genome completeness for the draft assembly, measured or inferred after assembly and expressed as a fraction from 0.0 to 1.0. Use to summarize how much of the expected genome was recovered.

Estimated contamination level in the draft genome assembly, measured after assembly and expressed as a fraction from 0.0 to 1.0. Use to summarize foreign sequence content in the derivative genome product.

File path, URI, or object-storage location where the draft genome sequence is stored; example: s3://bucket/assemblies/GNM-001.fna.gz or /data/assemblies/sample1.fasta. Record the retrieval location for the assembled genome artifact.

bgc_prediction.reasoning: The bgc_prediction node is a Process node, so I included only the computational method used to detect biosynthetic gene clusters, the software identity, key detection parameters, and a process-level quality indicator. I excluded draft genome properties because those belong to the upstream Derivative node, and I excluded the predicted cluster catalog itself because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to predict biosynthetic gene clusters from the assembled genome; example: antiSMASH. Record the computational tool that performed cluster detection.
Version of the BGC prediction software used during this step; example: 7.0.0. Record the exact version to support reproducibility of cluster detection.

Repository or distribution source for the BGC detection software, recorded for reproducibility; examples: GitHub URL, Bioconda package name, or container registry reference. Use to identify the implementation used in prediction.

Version of the reference database or rule set used by the BGC predictor, recorded at run time; example: antiSMASH built-in database release or profile set version. Use to capture the reference knowledge base applied during detection.

Minimum genomic length in base pairs required for a predicted biosynthetic gene cluster to be reported, configured during the detection step; typical values vary by pipeline and may be a few thousand base pairs. Record the length threshold used to call clusters.

Sensitivity or confidence setting used by the BGC predictor, recorded as a process parameter; examples: relaxed, default, or stringent, depending on software options. Use to describe how aggressively clusters were called.
Overall quality indicator for the BGC prediction step, assessed after detection completes; allowed values summarize whether the cluster calling output was usable for downstream mapping and analysis.

predicted_bgc_catalog.reasoning: The predicted_bgc_catalog node is a Derivative node, so I included only computed outputs describing the cluster set itself: catalog identity, number of clusters, coordinate/span summaries, cluster-type composition, and storage/access details. md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the predicted biosynthetic gene cluster catalog; string format example: BGC-CAT-001. Assigned after BGC prediction and used to track the cluster set into mapping and integrated analyses.
Number of predicted biosynthetic gene clusters in the catalog, counted after BGC prediction. Use as a summary of the derivative cluster set size.
Total genomic span in base pairs covered by all predicted clusters in the catalog, summed across cluster boundaries after prediction. Use to summarize the aggregate size of the cluster set.

Average predicted biosynthetic gene cluster length in base pairs, computed from the catalog after prediction; typical values often range from a few thousand to tens of thousands of base pairs. Use as a size summary of the cluster set.
High-level classes of predicted biosynthetic gene clusters present in the catalog, derived from the prediction output; examples include NRPS, PKS, terpene, and siderophore classes.

File path, URI, or object-storage location where the predicted cluster catalog is stored; example: s3://bucket/bgc_catalog/BGC-CAT-001.tsv or /data/bgcs/catalog.tsv. Record the retrieval location for the derivative cluster table or file.

Overall quality indicator for the predicted BGC catalog, assessed after prediction and curation; allowed values summarize whether the cluster set is sufficiently reliable for downstream mapping and annotation.

bgc_mapping.reasoning: The bgc_mapping node is a Process node, so I included only the computational mapping operation parameters and software identity, plus a process-level quality indicator for the mapping step. I excluded draft genome and predicted cluster catalog properties because those belong to upstream Derivative nodes, and I excluded the mapped location output itself because that belongs to the downstream Derivative node. md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to map predicted biosynthetic gene clusters onto the draft genome coordinates; example: antiSMASH or a genome coordinate mapping utility. Record the computational tool that performed the mapping step.
Version of the mapping software used during this step; example: 7.0.0. Record the exact version to support reproducibility of cluster location mapping.

Repository or distribution source for the mapping software, recorded for reproducibility; examples: GitHub URL, Bioconda package name, or container registry reference. Use to identify the implementation used in mapping.

Coordinate system used when mapping clusters onto the draft genome, recorded at process time; examples: contig-based or genome-based coordinates. Use to document how positions were represented during mapping.

Number of base pairs added on either side of each predicted cluster when generating mapped genomic locations, configured during the mapping step; typical values 0-5000 bp. Use to capture neighborhood context included in the mapped intervals.
Granularity of the mapping output, recorded as a process setting; examples: single-locus, interval-based, or neighborhood-based mapping. Use to describe how precisely cluster locations were reported.

Overall quality indicator for the BGC mapping process, assessed after coordinate assignment; allowed values summarize whether the mapping produced reliable genomic locations for downstream gene annotation and integrated analysis.

mapped_bgc_locations.reasoning: The mapped_bgc_locations node is a Derivative node, so I included only computed location outputs: the mapped interval identity, coordinate representation, neighborhood span, context size, and storage/access details. I excluded mapping software and parameters because those belong to the upstream bgc_mapping Process node, and I excluded gene-level annotations and integrated analysis outputs because those belong to later nodes. I also avoided previously generated shared technical fields such as file_format, file_size_bytes, read_count, storage_uri, and quality_score_summary due to the DAG-wide collision constraint.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for each mapped biosynthetic gene cluster location record; string format example: BGCLOC-001. Assigned after mapping and used to track the cluster interval into annotation and integrated analysis.
Identifier of the predicted biosynthetic gene cluster associated with this mapped location; string format example: BGC-001. Record the link back to the upstream cluster prediction result.
Draft genome contig identifier on which the biosynthetic gene cluster is mapped; string format example: contig_12. Record the assembly contig containing the cluster interval.

Start coordinate in base pairs for the mapped biosynthetic gene cluster on the draft genome contig, recorded in the derivative mapping output; typical values are positive integers from 1 upward. Use the 1-based interval start position.

End coordinate in base pairs for the mapped biosynthetic gene cluster on the draft genome contig, recorded in the derivative mapping output; typical values are positive integers greater than the start coordinate. Use the 1-based interval end position.

Total base-pair span of the genomic neighborhood reported around the mapped cluster, computed after adding flanking context to the cluster boundary; typical values range from 0 to several tens of thousands of base pairs. Use to describe how much surrounding sequence was retained in the mapping derivative.

Number of genes included in the mapped neighborhood context for the cluster, counted in the derivative output after interval expansion. Use to summarize the amount of local genomic context associated with the mapped cluster.

File path, URI, or object-storage location where the mapped BGC location table or file is stored; example: s3://bucket/mapped_bgc_locations/BGCLOC-001.tsv or /data/bgc_mapping/locations.tsv. Record the retrieval location for the derivative mapping result.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software used to assign putative functions to genes within biosynthetic gene clusters; example: Prokka. Record the computational tool that performed the gene annotation step.
Version of the gene annotation software used during this step; example: 1.14.6. Record the exact version to support reproducibility of gene function assignment.

Repository or distribution source for the gene annotation software, recorded for reproducibility; examples: GitHub URL, Bioconda package name, or container registry reference. Use to identify the implementation used in annotation.

Name of the reference database or annotation resource used to assign gene functions; examples: UniProt, Pfam, TIGRFAMs, or custom BGC-specific database. Record the knowledge source used during annotation.

Version or release date of the reference database used for gene annotation, recorded at run time; examples: database release number or YYYY-MM version. Use to capture the exact annotation reference set.

Maximum E-value threshold used to accept gene function assignments, configured during annotation; typical values range from 1e-3 to 1e-10 depending on pipeline stringency. Record the cutoff applied in this step.

Minimum confidence score or support threshold required to report a gene annotation, recorded during gene annotation; typical values depend on software and may be 0.5-0.95 on a normalized scale. Use to document calling stringency.

Overall quality indicator for the gene annotation process, assessed after functional assignment; allowed values summarize whether the annotations were sufficiently reliable for downstream interpretation of cluster genetics.

annotated_cluster_genes.reasoning: The annotated_cluster_genes node is a Derivative node, so I included only computed gene-level annotation outputs and storage details. md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the annotated gene set within biosynthetic clusters; string format example: BGCGENE-001. Assigned after gene annotation and used to track the annotation table into integrated analysis.

Identifier of the annotated gene within the draft genome or cluster interval; string format example: gene_1234 or locus_tag. Record the gene-level key used to connect function calls to the sequence feature.

Putative function assigned to the gene based on the annotation pipeline, recorded as a gene-level derivative output; examples: adenylation enzyme, ketosynthase, tailoring enzyme, transporter, or regulator.

Protein family or domain class associated with the annotated gene product, recorded from the annotation output; examples: NRPS_A, PKS_KS, ABC_transporter, or LuxR_family. Use to summarize gene product classification.
Confidence score for the assigned gene function, computed by the annotation pipeline or curated from supporting evidence; typical range 0.0-1.0. Use to quantify reliability of the functional call.

Evidence category supporting the gene annotation, recorded from the annotation output or curation; examples: homology, domain_hit, motif_hit, manual_curation, or mixed_evidence. Use to document how the function was inferred.

File path, URI, or object-storage location where the annotated cluster gene table is stored; example: s3://bucket/annotations/BGCGENE-001.tsv or /data/annotations/cluster_genes.tsv. Record the retrieval location for the derivative annotation result.

md_schema.descr: Chemical extraction method used to recover bacterial culture metabolites, recorded for the metabolite extraction step; examples: liquid-liquid extraction, solid-phase extraction, or solvent extraction. Primary solvent used during metabolite extraction, recorded at process time; examples: ethyl acetate, methanol, butanol, or chloroform. Use to document the chemistry used to recover antibiotic-containing compounds.

Duration of solvent contact or extraction time, measured in minutes from initiation to separation; typical range 5-1440. Record the time applied during the chemical extraction step.
Number of repeated extraction cycles performed on the bacterial culture, recorded during the process; typical values 1-5. Use to describe how thoroughly metabolites were recovered.

Overall quality indicator for the metabolite extraction process, assessed after crude extract recovery; allowed values summarize whether the extract was sufficiently concentrated and clean for analytical chemistry.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared chemical extract; string format example: EXT-001. Assigned after extraction and used to link the material to downstream LC-MS profiling.
